1.why: Server-side authorization derives account settings strictly from the session's authenticated user ID.

2.why: Verification codes are bound strictly to specific sessions and individual user secrets, so they do not work across different accounts.

3.why: Other active sessions for the user remain in the sessions map and continue functioning after MFA is enabled.

4.why: TOTP secrets are AES-GCM encrypted and backup codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes.

5.why: Crypto.getRandomValues is used to generate keys, seeds, backup codes, and session tokens.

6.why: Session tokens use HttpOnly cookies and no sensitive credentials or tokens are persisted in browser storage.

7.why: Server-side validation functions check and sanitize email, phone, OTP, and backup input using regular expressions.

8.why: Dynamic values rendered into the UI use safe textContent DOM assignments alongside strict Content Security Policy nonces.

9.why: Redirects are restricted to an explicit internal allow-list (the root path '/') and internal local HTTPS endpoints.

10.why: Security headers CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors are set on standard responses.

11.why: Session cookies explicitly set the HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: Server responses return generic error messages without stack traces, and sensitive tokens/seeds are excluded from URLs and server logs.

13.why: Identity codes, TOTP counter windows, and backup codes are invalidated upon use and enforce limited lifetimes.

14.why: Failure limits are tracked per feature, triggering temporary lockouts upon repeated invalid attempts.

15.why: Session tokens are rotated on authentication state changes, expire after idle and absolute limits, and are deleted on logout.
